input.prompt:
A real night street photograph in a dense city entertainment district with giant digital billboards and street-level screens: A slim two-sided digital kiosk totem stands on the wet pavement of the square, giant white screens on the towers behind.

The output is one single photograph, portrait 4:5.

Composition A, centred and symmetric: the design surface sits on the centre line, square to the camera, with even space on both sides; strong verticals and horizontals run parallel to the frame. Shot: Camera at totem height, 85mm lens, f/2.8, square to its face. The totem fills about 45 percent of the frame height on the centre line, sharp; the giant screens behind are soft out of focus; a subtle drizzle; the street glistens. Nobody is in frame.

Place: A dense city entertainment square at night: tall towers stacked with giant LED screens, wet asphalt and pavements, or a light fresh snowfall where the shot says; the weather is always subtle and real. Every screen in the square is a clean geometric shape with crisp edges and every screen shows a plain white full-screen image, ready for a design; no colour, text, logos or pictures on any screen.

Light: Night lit by the giant white screens: cool clean light spills across the wet streets and facades; small warm accents from traffic lights, street lamps and marquee bulbs; clean air, no smoke.

Palette and grade: Deep near-black night, glowing pure white screens, wet asphalt reflections, a few small red, amber and yellow accents from traffic and street lights. The same grade on every image of the collection.

Real: this is a product mockup photograph of a giant digital billboard, so the design surface is the hero: it is large in the frame and the camera is close enough that it dominates. It is a real place on a real wet night, shot from a real vantage point. The design surface faces the camera almost square-on, within about 15 degrees, so it reads flat and undistorted; its four edges run parallel to the edges of the photograph, a true rectangle, never a trapezoid or keystone; flat things on a table are shot from nearly straight above. Only the objects named in the shot are in frame. The hero screen is crisp at its edges and corners, with no bloom around it. The city is detailed and lived-in: wet kerbs, street furniture, traffic lights, awnings and fire escapes in true scale; the hero surface named in the shot is clear, sharp and generous in the frame, and the giant screens behind are never thin strips. Each screen is one simple plain rectangle, a single clean panel, never complex, curved, split or oddly shaped. Traffic moves naturally at uneven spacing, never lined up in neat rows.

Design surface: EVERY SCREEN, LIGHTBOX AND POSTER IN THE FRAME IS PLAIN WHITE: screens glow bright and clean, posters are matte paper-white, each a crisp rectangle with sharp corners; nothing printed on them and nothing crossing them.

Finish: Shot on a full-frame camera at night like real street photography: fine natural grain, true deep blacks, crisp highlights without bloom; real, never a render, never cyberpunk.

Avoid: a face, chin, lips or profile, logos, letters or brand names anywhere, any image or text on the design surface, tiny people in the street, halation, bloom or glow around the screen, smoke or haze, a sci-fi or 3D render look.
